answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each new identity climb a trellis of verified useful work, where the difficulty rises with every additional identity created in a short window, so a single operator spinning up a swarm faces a ferrous wall of real compute cost rather than free keys. Honest agents pass one modest checkpoint and then work normally, while a lagoon of fake accounts stalls at the rising steps, because forging a thousand identities would require a thousand times the proven effort, not just a thousand names.
